Scoring rules: score 0 requires no MWT reports and missing HSE Plan; that is not applicable because MWT reports exist.

Score 6 and 10 both require a verified % realisasi MWT (>=50% for 6, 100% for 10) and quantified MoM monthly coverage (>=50% for 6, 100% for 10). Because the approved HSE Plan with scheduled MWT (the denominator) is not available, % realisasi cannot be calculated; therefore the criteria for 6 or 10 cannot be deterministically met.

Available evidence (signed MWT reports, delegation, recurring meetings) demonstrates some senior-management involvement but is insufficiently complete or auditable to confirm consistent implementation per SR-1 thresholds; this aligns with the 'SKOR 3' description ('keterlibatan ada tapi sangat terbatas').

Given the jurors' inputs and the scoring rules, the conservative and rules-compliant recommendation is SKOR 3. This avoids over-crediting incomplete evidence while recognizing documented senior-management activity.

Requires review: to consider upgrading to 6 (or 10) the following must be supplied: the approved HSE Plan with MWT schedule; mapping of scheduled vs performed MWTs (to compute % realisasi); monthly MoM log to compute % bulan dengan MoM; complete MWT reports with signatures and follow-ups; and for score 10, HSE reward and sosialisasi/campaign evidence plus program/delegation documentation as required.

Because the policy exists and there is no definitive proof that coverage = 0%, SKOR 3 is the more appropriate application of the written scoring rules.

The available evidence (policies, HSE Plan, meeting minutes, performance forms, some signatures) demonstrates governance and activity but lacks the mandatory per-worker proof (attendance, commitments, test results) required to reach higher scores (6 or 10).
Given the two jurors supporting SKOR 3, the rule text that cites missing test evaluation as a SKOR 3 condition, and the lack of explicit 0% coverage evidence, the recommended score is 3.

Two jurors (Evidence and HSE) agree there is clear training activity (matrix, certificates, and an 83% realization metric) which supports a non-zero score; the Compliance juror stresses that missing mandatory numeric fields and verifiable links force a zero if strict proof is required.

The available 83% realization metric supports that % compliance for some training activity is >=50% and <100%, but it is not explicitly labeled as '% compliance K3LL formal' and there is no separate documented '% compliance Technical formal'—both are required by SR-3.2 for awarding score 6.

The single dissenting juror scored 3 because mandatory quantitative metrics (coverage %, column completeness, explicit stage coverage) were not documented/validated; while that point is valid, the substantive presence of documented analyses and active mitigations outweighs a minimal-score classification.

SKOR 10 cannot be recommended because all mandatory SKOR 10 conditions are not met: no validated 100% column completeness, no 100% HIRADC socialization coverage, no explicit evidence of all three stages covered, and no partner audits/subcontractor initiation evidence.

Given the documented risk assessments, procedures for high-risk tasks, and implemented controls, the evidence best matches the SR-4.1 description for SKOR 6 (identifikasi memadai, mitigasi dilakukan, procedures for high-risk present) despite missing numeric verifications.

Requires review: additional documentary validation is recommended to confirm % completeness of Risk Register columns, % HIRADC coverage, explicit stage coverage (mobilisasi/operasi/commissioning), partner audit reports, and signed/dated field inspection evidence — these could raise the score to 10 if fully satisfied.

Documentation quality issues (truncated files, missing attachments, limited keyword hits) reduce verifiability and justify a moderate confidence rather than high confidence despite juror unanimity.

Per SR-4.6, score 3 is appropriate when a security program exists but key certification metrics or MoU(s) are missing or inadequate (e.g., % First Aid or Fire Fighting certificates <50% or MoU RS absent). To reach 10, all of the above plus 100% ERT certification and routine monitoring/incident logs are required.

Given unanimous juror agreement and the absence of conflicting evidence, the final recommended score is 3. However, because mandatory evidence is missing or unverifiable, further review with the requested documents is required to reassess and potentially upgrade the score.

Confidence (0.66) reflects moderate agreement among jurors (0.8, 0.72, 0.45) and unanimous scoring, tempered by missing critical documents that limit certainty about sustained CSR management.

Requires review: true — because mandatory VR-5.2 fields are missing and the assessor should request/upload the listed missing evidence (equipment listing with certificate numbers/expiry, pre-use forms, maintenance realization metrics, and monitoring reports) to validate a higher score.

Meskipun ada prosedur dan beberapa form MOC yang terisi, kriteria SR-5.3 untuk skor 6 mengharuskan: cakupan ketiga jenis perubahan, form MOC diimplementasikan dengan risk assessment, DAN % kelengkapan form ≥80%. % kelengkapan dan bukti risk assessment per form tidak diverifikasi dalam bukti yang diserahkan.

evidence_found: Existence of ERP/MER and related SOPs (Logindo MER, vessel emergency plans, SOP P/QHSE/13).

Multiple jurors independently concluded ERP and drills exist but mandatory certification/checklist evidence is not fully verifiable.

reasoning: All three jurors independently scored 3 and cited the same core facts: ERP and drills exist but mandatory certification and complete checklist/documentation are missing or unverifiable.

Per SR-5.4, score 3 applies when ERP exists but ERT is not fully certified OR drills lack structured evaluation; available evidence matches these conditions (ERP present, but 100% ERT First Aid/Fire Fighting certification not shown and drill evaluation/observer documentation inconsistent).

Higher scores (6 or 10) require demonstrable 100% certification, drill realisation thresholds, and comprehensive drill evaluation/observer reports — these mandatory items are not evidenced or are incomplete, so upgrading is not justified.
Average juror confidence is ~0.71, supporting moderate confidence in the assigned score while acknowledging data gaps.

Requires review: because several critical documents are missing, truncated, or lack expiry checks, a targeted document request (certificates, full rosters, complete drill reports, LSA/FFA checklists) could materially change the score if they demonstrate compliance with SR-5.4.
Recommendation: finalize score = 3 now, and trigger document follow-up to verify missing mandatory items for potential reassessment.

evidence_found: Leading indicators tracked (HSSE Meeting, Inspeksi HSSE, JSA, Tool Box Meeting, Permit To Work, Training HSSE) documented in KPI/templates and monthly reports.
Lagging indicators defined in KPI documents (FIR, LWDC, RWDC, MTC) and monthly reports showing zero incidents for sampled months.
Monthly HSE Performance reports (Lampiran 22) covering Jan–Nov (multiple months documented), meeting the >=80% reporting threshold in the sample.
Monthly office–field HSE meetings documented (meeting minutes, MoM, action logs) across many months (Jan–Nov), supporting >=80% meeting frequency.
Safe man-hours evidence present (KPI documents listing total man-hours e.g., ~22,044/year and monthly breakdowns) and zero incident reporting for the period.
Field inspections, meeting minutes, and action logs showing implementation activity and corrective action tracking (though many actions remain open).
missing_evidence: Clear, consolidated HSE Plan file demonstrably listing both complete leading AND lagging indicators in one authoritative document (some jurors noted this was not explicitly identified).
100% monthly HSE Performance reports for the entire project duration (SR-6.1 requirement for score 10).
100% monthly MoM office–field meeting records for the entire project duration (SR-6.1 requirement for score 10).
Documented HSE Meeting between management and workers (MoM) for every month (management–worker meeting evidence not clearly present/complete).
Formal 'kajian perbaikan' (system-level review with analysis and recommendations to improve K3LL implementation) required for score 10.
Complete inspection reports explicitly demonstrating that field implementation matched the Rencana K3LL for all areas (some inspection evidence exists but not fully verifiable/complete).
Consistent denominators/context for some KPI calculations (some Lampiran 22 records lack man-hour denominators or clear context).
reasoning: All three jurors independently scored 6 with similar confidence levels and consistent reasoning: leading and lagging indicators are present, monthly reporting and meetings meet the >=80% threshold in the sampled months, and safe man-hours evidence exists.

SR-6.1 score-6 criteria are satisfied: HSE Plan elements (leading + lagging indicators) are represented in the evidence, >=80% monthly HSE Performance reports are present in the sample, >=80% monthly office–field meetings are documented, and safe man-hours evidence is provided.

Score-10 criteria are not met: mandatory 100% requirements (100% monthly reports and 100% monthly meetings), documented management–worker HSE meeting MoMs for every month, a formal kajian perbaikan, and complete verification inspections against the Rencana K3LL are not fully demonstrated in the evidence.

Data quality and completeness issues (inconsistent audit reporting, open corrective actions, missing denominators/context in some records, and absent explicit system-improvement documentation) reduce certainty that higher thresholds for score 10 have been achieved.

Given unanimous juror agreement on score 6, and the identified evidence gaps preventing score 10, the recommended final score is 6. Confidence is set at 0.62 (average of juror confidences adjusted for noted evidence quality issues).

evidence_found: Multiyear incident statistics provided covering 2022–2025 (4 years of data).
Annual incident counts reported as zero recordable incidents for each year in the available period.
Leading indicator activities documented: inspections, JSA, toolbox talks, permit-to-work records, meeting minutes.
Operational gaps noted in evidence: inconsistent audit delivery, some months with 0% audits, emergency drills sometimes below target, open corrective actions.
Validation/keyword search returned low coverage (approx. 2/8 VR-6.2 keywords found) indicating limited documentation against checkpoint keywords.
Juror assessments (Compliance, Evidence, HSE) unanimously interpreted the evidence as data-present but not demonstrating an improving TRIR/LTI trend or mature near-miss culture.
missing_evidence: Nilai TRIR atau LTI rate per tahun (explicit calculations for each year).
Jumlah near miss report vs actual incident per year (near-miss counts and ratio).
Incident records with full detail per incident: tanggal, jenis, lokasi, jumlah korban, LTI flag.
Statistik insiden ≥ 5 tahun (extension of dataset to meet SR-6.2 top-score requirement).
Evidence demonstrating a stable year-on-year decreasing TRIR/LTI trend (required for score 6→10 differentiation).
Documentary evidence required for score 10 (HSE Plan with KPIs, HSE Monthly Performance ≥5 years, inspection logs, safe man hours evidence) or closure evidence for outstanding corrective actions.
reasoning: All three jurors scored 3 and provided similar reasoning: multiyear data exist (2022–2025) but do not meet SR-6.2 requirements for higher scores.

Per SR-6.2, score 3 applies when data exist but trend does not show improvement (or data <2 years). Here the available 4-year series is flat (zero incidents) rather than a demonstrable year‑on‑year decrease in TRIR/LTI, so it does not meet the 'tren membaik' condition for score 6 or the ≥5-year + mature-reporting conditions for score 10.

Key mandatory fields are missing or not verifiable (notably TRIR/LTI per year and near-miss vs actual incident counts), reducing ability to validate an improving lagging metric or mature reporting culture.
Leading indicator evidence is positive but insufficient to override the absence of validated lagging trends and near-miss reporting required by SR-6.2 for higher scores.
Given unanimous juror agreement, consistent application of SR-6.2, and the documented evidence gaps, the conservative and rule-consistent final recommendation is score 3.

To raise the score in future assessments: supply explicit TRIR/LTI calculations per year, extend incident statistics to ≥5 years, provide detailed incident logs and near-miss counts demonstrating a mature reporting culture (near-miss ≥5× actual incidents), and close outstanding corrective actions / standardize audits and drills.

evidence_found: Monthly HSE performance reports (2022�2025) showing KPI tables and trends
Lagging indicators reported as zero (no LTI/fatality/MTC/spills) across covered periods
Leading-indicator records for many activities (HSSE meetings, inspections, JSA, toolbox talks, permit-to-work) with month-by-month entries
Meeting minutes (MoM) field3 office and HSE meeting minutes, attendance lists and safety talk records
Inspection reports and corrective action logs (open and closed actions documented)
KPI definitions/formulas and man-hours tables
missing_evidence: Consolidated per-indicator % pencapaian leading indicator (numeric, auditable table against HSE Plan targets)
Consolidated per-indicator % pencapaian lagging indicator (numeric, auditable table against HSE Plan targets)
Complete HSE Plan table showing leading+lagging targets vs realizations in single auditable matrix
Company-wide evidence that KPI were communicated to all organizational levels (e.g., memos/distribution lists/sign-off logs)
Consolidated evidence of safe man-hours supporting 'zero accident' claim (single summary)
Formal root-cause analyses linking causes to specific unmet KPIs for underperforming leading programs
reasoning: Two of three jurors (Compliance and HSE) independently scored 3 and provide consistent reasoning that leading indicators are not uniformly 100% while lagging indicators show zero incidents; Evidence juror scored 6 but flagged key mandatory consolidation gaps that prevent full validation to a higher score.

SR-6.3 mapping: score 10 requires 100% leading AND 100% lagging AND zero accident AND documented KPI communication to all levels. That full set of conditions is not met (leading not uniformly 100%, KPI communication to all levels not fully evidenced).

Score 6 requires both leading and lagging = 100% (and any accidents only keparahan I). Leading evidence shows variability (many activities at/above target but some key leading programs repeatedly low, with monthly realizations as low as 4�239%); therefore the strict criterion for 6 is not satisfied.

Score 3 applies when indicators are partially achieved (50%
<100%) or when there is a keparahan II accident. The documented monthly overall compliance trend (reported ~82%�200% across months) and specific underperforming leading programs place performance in the 'partial achievement' band, matching score 3.
There is clear evidence of zero accidents (supports not assigning 0), but missing consolidated numeric achievement tables and incomplete proof of KPI communication prevent upgrading to 6 or 10.

Given the juror majority, the documented evidence, and the mandatory-field gaps that reduce upward confidence, the conservative, rules-aligned recommendation is score = 3 with moderate confidence and further reviewer follow-up requested to obtain the missing consolidated documentation before reconsidering a higher score.

results.folder_name: 6.4 Investigasi dan Tindak Lanjut Insiden K3LL
evidence_found: Dokumen prosedur investigasi insiden: MJM-HSEP-004.x dan Logindo P/QHSE/08 (mencakup ruang lingkup, definisi, dan panduan komposisi tim investigasi).

Bukti Safety Stand Down (laporan/absensi/agenda) dan persentase realisasi Safety Stand Down sesuai jadwal.
% coverage sosialisasi cara pelaporan (harus terkuantifikasi; untuk skor 6 minimal >=80%, untuk skor 10 =100%).
Bukti formulir pelaporan + alur proses (flowchart) dan/atau bagan tim investigasi yang lengkap dan terlampir dalam prosedur (jika belum jelas).
Sertifikat kompetensi tim investigasi yang valid dan tidak expired (masa berlaku/divalidasi).
Bukti bahwa pekerja mampu mengenali unsafe act/unsafe condition (hasil inspeksi/observasi/monitoring).
Bukti zero incident selama proyek (untuk skor 10) — tidak tersedia.
Dokumen yang korup/terbaca rusak (Doc 6) perlu diganti agar evaluasi lengkap dapat dilakukan.
reasoning: Semua tiga juror (Compliance, Evidence, HSE) independen merekomendasikan skor 3 dengan confidence sedang-tinggi; tidak ada konflik skor antar juror.

Skor 3 sesuai dengan SR-6.4 apabila prosedur investigasi ada tetapi implementasi/instrumen pendukung atau tim tidak bersertifikat/valid atau tidak ada bukti laporan investigasi (prosedur ada tetapi 0 implementasi atau tim tidak bersertifikat).

Terdapat prosedur tertulis dan aktivitas QHSE parsial, namun tidak ada bukti dokumenter laporan investigasi/RCFA, tidak ada bukti Safety Stand Down yang memenuhi persyaratan, dan sertifikat pelatihan tidak diverifikasi masa berlakunya — sehingga persyaratan untuk skor 6 atau 10 tidak terpenuhi.
Skor 0 tidak berlaku karena prosedur ada; skor 6/10 tidak dapat diberikan karena ketiadaan bukti implementasi, validitas sertifikat, coverage sosialisasi, dan bukti Safety Stand Down/zero incident.

Rekomendasi tindakan: upload laporan investigasi/RCFA, sertifikat terkini yang menunjukkan masa berlaku, bukti sosialisasi dengan persentase coverage (absensi + materi), dan dokumentasi Safety Stand Down untuk memungkinkan kenaikan skor pada review selanjutnya.
